description:
Apollo.io is the leading go-to-market solution for revenue teams, trusted by over 500,000 companies and millions of users globally, from rapidly growing startups to some of the world's largest enterprises. Founded in 2015, the company is one of the fastest growing companies in SaaS, raising approximately $250 million to date and valued at $1.6 billion. Apollo.io provides sales and marketing teams with easy access to verified contact data for over 210 million B2B contacts and 35 million companies worldwide, along with tools to engage and convert these contacts in one unified platform. By helping revenue professionals find the most accurate contact information and automating the outreach process, Apollo.io turns prospects into customers. Apollo raised a series D in 2023 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and more, and counts the former President and COO of Hubspot, JD Sherman, among its board members.

About the role

Apollo is hiring a Senior Data Scientist, Growth to own the data behind how new users become activated, paying, and retained customers. You will sit inside the Growth and Acquisition org, embedded with the product teams that runfree-to-paid conversion, retention, pricing and packaging, onboarding, activation, and expansion.

This is not a reporting seat. You will be accountable for moving growth metrics, using experimentation, causal analysis, and modelling to find which changes actually produce paying, retained teams, and to stop the ones that do not. You will partner daily with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers, and you will set the measurement standard for how Growth decides what to ship.

Apollo is a go-to-market platform for revenue teams. Growth runs on a large self-serve funnel, and a small lift at the top or in the middle compounds quickly into revenue.

What you will do

  • Own measurement for one or more Growth product areas: Help foster a culture of data-driven decision-making and continuous improvement within growth product teams.
  • Define the north-star metric, the leading indicators, and the guardrails for each.
  • Run experiments end to end: hypothesis, power and sample size, exposure logging, sample ratio checks, readout, and a clear ship, iterate, or kill call. Flag when a win in one segment is paid for by a loss in another.
  • Connect early user behavior to downstream revenue. Work out which first actions predict paid retention, then turn that into leading indicators a team can read inside a sprint instead of waiting a quarter.
  • Diagnose funnel and cohort movement. Separate real change from instrumentation bugs and metric redefinitions, and backfill history when a definition changes.
  • Size opportunities in ARR before the roadmap is set, so Product Managers can prioritize on expected impact and stop work that is not paying back.
  • Own the quality of Growth instrumentation: event taxonomy, metric definitions, and the dashboards leadership uses in recurring business reviews.
  • Use AI-assisted analytics tooling to take routine reporting off your plate, and spend that time on experiments, deep dives, and decisions.

What you bring

  • 5+ years in product or growth data science at a product-led, self-serve SaaS company, with a record of changing what a product team shipped because of your analysis.
  • 0-to-1 launches where the metrics had to be defined before any baseline existed.
  • Deep experimentation practice in a self-serve funnel. You know how to handle sample ratio mismatch, variance reduction, sequential looks, multiple comparisons, and thin traffic in smaller segments. You also know when a clean A/B test is not possible and can use holdouts, difference-in-differences, or synthetic controls instead.
  • Working knowledge of the free-to-paid journey: how activation gets defined, how time-to-value is measured, how trials, feature gates, and upgrade prompts create purchase moments, and how first-invoice value and expansion are affected by what you steer people toward.
  • Judgment about metrics. You can tell when a metric is measuring activity rather than durable behavior, and when a retention number moved because of an instrumentation change rather than user behavior.
  • Expert SQL, plus Python or R for modeling. Hands-on experience with propensity or uplift models, survival and retention curves, and lifetime value.
  • Experience with a product analytics tool such as Amplitude, Mixpanel, or Heap, and a warehouse-based notebook or BI environment.
  • A habit of tying work to revenue. You can describe a metric you moved and what it was worth in ARR.
  • Comfort telling a Product Manager that a favorite idea lost, showing the evidence, and still being the first person they call for the next planning cycle.
  • A degree in statistics, applied math, economics, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Nice to have

  • Pricing and packaging experimentation, including annual versus monthly billing, plan tier steering, and usage-limit design.
  • Experience measuring lifecycle email and in-app messaging programs alongside product experiments.
  • Paid acquisition or marketing attribution exposure, including channel-level incrementality.
  • Experience measuring AI-powered product features, including how users adopt them and how they affect retention.

The listed Pay Range reflects the total cash compensation inclusive of annual base salary and annual bonus as applicable. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonus target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Apollo and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity; company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; at least 10 paid holidays per year, flex PTO, and parental leave; employee assistance program and wellbeing benefits; global travel coverage; life/AD&D/STD/LTD insurance; FSA/HSA and medical, dental, and vision benefits.

Tier 1 Pay Range (San Francisco, New York City, Seattle)
$180,000—$240,000 USD
Tier 2 Pay Range (All other US Locations)
$160,000—$220,000 USD

We are AI Native

Apollo.io is an AI-native company built on a culture of continuous improvement. We’re on the front lines of driving productivity for our customers—and we expect the same mindset from our team. If you're energized by finding smarter, faster ways to get things done using AI and automation, you'll thrive here.

Why You’ll Love Working at Apollo

At Apollo, we’re driven by a shared mission: to help our customers unlock their full revenue potential. That’s why we take extreme ownership of our work, move with focus and urgency, and learn voraciously to stay ahead.

We invest deeply in your growth, ensuring you have the resources, support, and autonomy to own your role and make a real impact. Collaboration is at our core—we’re all for one, meaning you’ll have a team across departments ready to help you succeed. We encourage bold ideas and courageous action, giving you the freedom to experiment, take smart risks, and drive big wins.

If you’re looking for a place where your work matters, where you can push boundaries, and where your career can thrive—Apollo is the place for you. 

Learn more here!
